semantic_correction.stem: A client with stable chronic heart failure asks which lifestyle habits should remain part of long-term self-care. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Stay active within the individualized plan, avoid tobacco, follow the recommended heart-healthy eating pattern, and discuss alcohol use with the health care team.
options.B: Because medications control heart-failure physiology, lifestyle changes are mainly optional once symptoms stabilize; activity and diet can return to usual habits.
options.C: Limit activity to routine daily tasks and avoid structured exercise, because chronic heart failure generally makes planned physical activity unsafe.
options.D: Continue usual smoking or alcohol habits if symptoms are controlled, because these behaviors no longer meaningfully affect chronic heart-failure self-care.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current American Heart Association heart-failure guidance recommends ongoing appropriate physical activity, tobacco avoidance, and a heart-healthy eating pattern as part of chronic heart-failure self-care. It also advises clients to discuss alcohol use with their health care professional. The AHA's 2026 dietary guidance states that people who do not drink alcohol should not start and that those who do drink should limit intake. B is incorrect because lifestyle measures remain part of long-term management alongside medications. C is incorrect because appropriate regular physical activity is encouraged and may be individualized through the health care or cardiac-rehabilitation team. D is incorrect because smoking and alcohol use remain relevant cardiovascular and heart-failure management issues even when symptoms are controlled.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Reinforce long-term heart-failure self-care through individualized physical activity, tobacco avoidance, a heart-healthy dietary pattern, and safe individualized counseling about alcohol use alongside prescribed therapy.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure; 2026 Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health — Top Things to Know
semantic_correction.source_version_date: AHA heart-failure lifestyle guidance current page accessed August 21, 2026; dietary scientific statement updated March 31, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Lifestyle Changes for Heart Failure — 'Quit smoking'; 'Be physically active': regular moderate-intensity activity and individualized activity planning with the health care/cardiac-rehabilitation team; 'Avoid or limit alcohol': discuss whether alcohol is appropriate with the health care professional; 'Eat for a healthy heart': follow an overall healthy eating pattern. 2026 Dietary Guidance — Top Things to Know, item 7: heart-healthy dietary pattern includes reduced sodium; if alcohol is not consumed, do not start, and if alcohol is consumed, limit intake.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Long-term heart-failure self-care includes individualized physical activity, tobacco avoidance, heart-healthy nutrition, and individualized counseling about alcohol use; these measures continue after diagnosis and complement medical therapy.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the extreme correct-answer length cue, retained current AHA long-term self-care guidance, and rebuilt all four options as parallel chronic-heart-failure lifestyle plans of comparable length.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests ongoing lifestyle self-management after heart-failure diagnosis with one clearly best answer and no correct-option length cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. Each component is directly supported by current AHA guidance and is framed as individualized long-term self-care rather than a substitute for prescribed therapy.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Stabilized symptoms do not make lifestyle measures optional; AHA guidance continues to recommend healthy activity, diet, and other habits as part of ongoing heart-failure management.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. AHA guidance encourages appropriate physical activity and individualized exercise planning rather than routine avoidance of structured activity in stable chronic heart failure.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Smoking and alcohol remain relevant to cardiovascular and heart-failure management; symptom control does not make these behaviors clinically irrelevant.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects current ongoing self-care guidance; B incorrectly makes lifestyle optional, C discourages appropriate activity, and D dismisses ongoing tobacco/alcohol risk.
cueing_check: The choices are tightly balanced in length (A 162, B 162, C 148, D 155 characters), use parallel lifestyle-plan language, and no option is uniquely detailed or conspicuously longer than the others.
